questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The nature, the fact that I could take some courses in danish, the city Reykjavik.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: overall a wonderful experience! The structure on campus could sometime have been better

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Sometimes a bit difficult. Just because the university didn't gave the information I needed. But also because there was just so much information to manage.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Information about where the classroom were.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: A bit more info and knowledge about where to get information could have been nice.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Really difficult! They didn't give any help with housing

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That no-one will help them finding it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I should register at a service desk at university. And I could pic up a student card within one week after,

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Some service persons helped me at the service desk

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was successful in registering the classes I wanted, but it was really sad that some of the classes overlapped, so I needed to skip the last part of some of the classes. A lot of other students had the same problem

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: make sure that the classes don't overlap because the host University will not let you know.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some very small classes (5 ECTS) had a lot of expectations and a lot of tests and requirements. I didn't always think that the amount of study work was proportional with the ECTS amount.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: One in 5 ects, one in 6 acts, one in 10 and another one in 10 ects

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More group work, a lot of reading material, only class teaching

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Being Icelandic, Nordic movies and identity, danish modern literature, Creative industries

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Creative industries because we had guest lectures from the art and creative industries from Iceland. It was really nice to combine the theory with specific cases.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Everything was just really expensive in Reykjavik, so all costed more than I expected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive than I thought.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A bio, fitness, student bar

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The student bar is cheap!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Going out in nature, do some trips out in the wonderful country.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be part of the mentor group, go to bars and cultural event during the week in town.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The Icelandic people are pretty closed, so you have to do your own outreach and not expect that you will get the information you need. You need to contact people for information.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The city in general is really cultural. I loved going to a place called Mengi which is a venue for upcoming artist in Reykjavik

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be patient with getting information, take advantage of the opportunities, remember to socialize, you will get friends from the whole world

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: you have to be proactive about borrowing books on campus, it's not something they tell you

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Taking a break from my everyday life and just do something really different! It gave me a lot of energy!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To tap into the Icelandic mentality of taking it easy and trust the process. And to accept not to know things.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just really recomment going on an exchange!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
